headline: SAUDI ARABIA UNVEILS 110M-TONNE RARE EARTH AND URANIUM FIND IN MADINAH — MA'ADEN SIGNS UP MP MATERIALS FOR US-BACKED CRITICAL METALS PROGRAM
snippet: Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman announced September 14 at the 70th IAEA General Conference in Vienna the discovery of approximately 110–114 million tonnes of rare earth-enriched and uranium-bearing ore at the Jabal Sayid project in the Madinah region — positioning it among the world's premier rare earth development sites. Saudi mining company Ma'aden has partnered with US-based MP Materials to develop rare earth mineral processing and uranium production capabilities, with the find directly tied to the US-Saudi civilian nuclear deal signed in July 2026 that laid the foundation for a decades-long, multibillion-dollar partnership.

headline: MINING LEADS CARNEY'S C$1T PITCH — 63 PROJECTS AT CANADA'S FIRST INVESTMENT SUMMIT AS BLACKROCK AND $70T IN ASSETS FILL THE ROOM
snippet: Canada's first-ever Canada Investment Summit opened September 14–15 in Toronto with PM Mark Carney pitching C$1 trillion in five-year investments to 100 global investors collectively overseeing more than $70 trillion in assets — mining commands the largest share of the 167-project prospectus at 63 projects, nearly double the 31 clean energy entries. BlackRock chairman Larry Fink and Temasek CEO Dilhan Pillay were among attendees as TD Bank committed C$150 billion across priority sectors, with critical minerals infrastructure accounting for a meaningful share of the projects on offer.

headline: BLUE JAY DRILLS 14.0M AT 6.15 G/T GOLD AND 124 G/T SILVER IN MAIDEN YUKON PROGRAM — HISTORIC MT. SKUKUM CUTS 57.4 G/T BONANZA INTERVAL
snippet: Blue Jay Gold Corp (TSX-V: JAY) reported September 14 the first assay results from its maiden 2026 diamond drill program at the Steller Gold Project in Yukon — hole SC26-003 returned 14.0 metres at 6.15 g/t Au and 124 g/t Ag (8.04 g/t AuEq) from 495 metres, including 10.5 metres at 7.84 g/t Au and 154 g/t Ag (10.19 g/t AuEq), a 32-metre down-plunge extension of a 2021 high-grade hit. A second hole on the historic Mt. Skukum mine site — producer of 77,790 oz from 1986–1988 — returned a 0.5-metre bonanza of 57.4 g/t Au, with assays pending on additional completed holes as mineralization remains open.

headline: SILVER ACADIA CLOSES PHASE 1 WITH 24.8M AT 329 G/T SILVER IN NEW BRUNSWICK — COPPER AT MILLSTREAM WIDENS THE SYSTEM TO 3KM
snippet: Silver Acadia Exploration Inc reported September 15 the final assay results from its 18-hole, 2,404-metre Phase 1 program at the Nicholas-Denys Silver Project in New Brunswick — highlight hole ND26-005 returned 24.8 metres at 328.9 g/t Ag, 1.0 g/t Au, 1.5% Zn, and 2.0% Pb from the Hachey Zone, while broad copper-bearing intervals were also intersected at the nearby Millstream Zone. Combined with earlier Phase 1 results including 7.1 metres at 396.8 g/t Ag and 2.38 g/t Au, the program has defined a mineralized corridor up to three kilometres long across the Hachey, Shaft, Dante, and Henry zones.

headline: WHITEHORSE COPPER EXPANDS — GLADIATOR HITS 21.2M AT 3.07% CU AND 1.19 G/T GOLD AT CUB EAST AS BLACK CUB TREND EXTENDS TO 1.5KM
snippet: Gladiator Metals Corp (TSX-V: GLAD) released further assay results September 15 from the Cub East target at its Whitehorse Copper Project in Yukon — best hole BCG-045 returned 21.2 metres at 3.07% Cu, 1.19 g/t Au, and 24.65 g/t Ag from 183 metres, while BCG-050 delivered 47.0 metres at 1.01% Cu. The high-grade core at Cub East is now confirmed over 350 metres of strike within the 1.5-kilometre Black Cub trend; a 50,000-metre 2026 program has five rigs rotating through the site with step-out drilling 600 metres southeast already encountering additional skarn mineralisation.

headline: LAHONTAN DRILLS 16.5M AT 2.72 G/T GOLD FROM HISTORIC HEAP LEACH PAD — NEVADA REPROCESSING PLAY TOPS GRADE EXPECTATIONS
snippet: Lahontan Gold Corp (TSX-V: LG) reported September 15 that ten Sonic drill holes targeting Heap Leach Pad Two at the Santa Fe Mine Project in Nevada returned grades substantially above prior expectations, with a highlight intercept of 16.5 metres at 2.72 g/t Au and 2.8 g/t Ag. Cyanide-extractable gold values averaged 43% of fire assay across the program, suggesting the historic heap leach material may be economically amenable to reprocessing — a low-capital-cost path to gold production from a past-producing Nevada asset.

headline: THE PERMITTING SHORTCUT NOBODY IS TALKING ABOUT — NORTHERN MINER'S CASE FOR OLD MINES AS CANADA'S FASTEST CRITICAL MINERALS PATH
snippet: A Northern Miner opinion piece argues that Canada's most viable near-term path to critical mineral supply runs through brownfield reopenings and legacy mine expansions — sites that already carry permits, infrastructure, tailings data, and geological knowledge that new greenfield projects won't replicate for 15–20 years. The argument carries particular weight as PM Carney simultaneously pitches C$1 trillion in mining investment at the Canada Investment Summit, and as provinces race to be competitive on permitting timelines that still average six years longer than in Australia.

headline: RECORD GOLD MINER PROFITS CAN'T CLOSE THE VALUATION GAP — GDXJ TRADES AT 16X P/E, A 41-QUARTER LOW DESPITE $41B CASH HOARDS
snippet: With Q2 2026 profits setting records despite a mid-quarter gold price dip, an analysis argues that record quarterly earnings — GDX top 25 operating cash flows surging 52.5% year-over-year to $17.2 billion and cash treasuries hitting a fresh record of $41.3 billion — only deepens the paradox that GDXJ constituents trade at historically cheap 16.1x trailing P/E, their lowest valuation in at least 41 quarters. The piece frames this as the clearest signal in years that institutional money remains underweight the sector, creating asymmetric upside for investors willing to hold through Fed-driven selling ahead of Wednesday's FOMC decision.
